column2: On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Suckling makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful.”
Al-raḍāʿah (“suckling”): with fatḥah on the rāʾ; nursing.
Tuḥarrimu (“makes unlawful”): with the rāʾ doubled and carrying kasrah, and ḍammah on its first letter.
“What birth makes unlawful”: the like of what it makes unlawful.
Suckling is like lineage in making things unlawful.

This is by consensus with regard to the prohibition of marriage and what follows from it, combining two related women [in marriage], the spreading of the prohibition between the suckled child and the children of the nursing woman, and treating them as relatives in permitting such things as looking, being alone together and travelling together—but not in the other rulings,

such as mutual inheritance, the obligation of maintenance and the like. Moreover, the prohibition mentioned is with respect to the nurse: her relatives become relatives of the suckled child; but as for the relatives of the suckled child, other than his children, there is no relationship between them and the nurse, so none of these rulings apply to them.
